# §5 Commerce Analytics — Highlight Candidates

1. **eCat captures 9.7% of $137.9M total business by GMV** — trending upward from ~5% in mid-2025 to 13.5% in April 2026. The 2.8x gap between GMV capture (9.7%) and order capture (3.5%) confirms reps use the platform for their most valuable transactions. [→ §commerce]
2. **327 unrealized market commitment items across four High Point markets** — April 2025 converted at 77.2%, but October 2025 dropped to 43.6% with 132 items still uncommitted. These are warm leads requiring re-engagement, not cold outreach. [→ §commerce]
3. **20 accounts show declining average unit prices, representing $8.9M in current-quarter business** — City Furniture (-33.3%), Koper Furniture (-74.9%), and Wayfair (-6.3%, $2.4M) lead the list. Pricing shifts may indicate competitive pressure, product substitution, or tier migration. [→ §commerce]
4. **Top-5 buyer concentration at just 12% of eCat GMV** — a healthy, diversified base with no single-account dependency risk. Wichita Furniture and Miskellys lead at $430K each. [→ §commerce]

## Priority Action Candidate
- **HIGH**: Re-engage the 132 unrealized commitment items from October 2025 High Point — now 8 months old, these represent explicit buying intent captured at market that is at risk of going cold. Converting even 50% of unrealized items at historical average prices could generate an estimated $200K+ in follow-through revenue [HYPOTHETICAL]. [→ §commerce]
